articles.title: Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace
articles.snippet: Official Claude Code Extension Compromise: Security Advisory | Phorion 🎉 Phorion ranked #1 in independent EDR telemetry evaluations. Learn more Features Detecting Threats Behavioral detection and threat hunting Protecting Endpoints File access controls and hash blocking Responding to Incidents Live response and device isolation Endpoint Visibility Deep telemetry via Apple's ESF Pricing About Us Blog Book a Demo October 30, 2026 Updated October 31, 2026 By Calum Hall Official Claude Code Extension Compromise: Security Advisory SSH Backdoor Cursor Marketplace VS Code macOS Linux Windows Threat Report TL;DR Phorion has detected a backdoor in the official Claude Code for VS Code extension bundle on the Cursor Marketplace that drops a persistent SSH backdoor across macOS, Linux, and Windows. This write-up focuses primarily on macOS, where the extension attempts to configure an SSH backdoor and establish persistence. Organisations should immediately review their environments for use of Claude Code for VSCode 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 and engage incident response where use of the extension is discovered. Update (31 October 2026): Cursor’s security notice now identifies versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 distributed through the Cursor Marketplace for macOS and Windows as affected. This advisory previously identified only 2.1.313 ; the affected-version guidance below has been updated accordingly. Phorion has discovered a compromise of the official Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace, where the backdoored extension bundle contains a persistent Secure Shell (SSH) backdoor. Cursor has removed the affected versions, 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 , from its marketplace. While the implant includes setup and persistence logic for macOS, Linux, and Windows , we’re going to focus primarily on macOS in this post, calling out the key differences and a few implementation bugs on the other platforms along the way. The Cursor Marketplace serves extensions for the Cursor editor. Because extensions run with the permissions of the IDE and the user running it, a backdoored extension gets immediate access to local files, source code, and developer tooling as soon as its module is loaded. Notably, Phorion has discovered a likely oversight in how the malware tries to turn on SSH. The setup logic assumes it can check the current Remote Login state without root privileges. When run as a standard user, systemsetup -getremotelogin prints an administrator-access error and exits with status 0 instead of returning Off . Because the script only tries to enable SSH if the output matches Off , it skips the enablement step entirely. On a Mac that doesn’t already have SSH running, that mistake breaks the inbound access path, even though the SSH keys and persistence still get dropped. In this post, we’ll walk through how the backdoor works, why that macOS check fails, and what to look for across your fleet. The goal of this payload is long-term interactive access

articles.summaryKo: 보안업체 Phorion이 Cursor Marketplace에 배포된 공식 Claude Code for VS Code 확장(버전 2.1.312, 2.1.313)에서 영구적인 SSH 백도어를 발견했다. 이 백도어는 macOS, Linux, Windows 전반에 걸쳐 지속성을 설정하도록 설계되었으며, 확장이 로드되는 즉시 IDE 권한으로 로컬 파일과 소스코드에 접근할 수 있게 한다. 다만 macOS에서는 권한 체크 로직의 오류로 인해 SSH가 이미 켜져 있지 않은 경우 활성화 단계가 실제로는 건너뛰어지는 버그가 확인됐다. Cursor는 해당 버전을 마켓플레이스에서 제거했으며, 기업들은 영향받은 버전 사용 여부를 즉시 점검해야 한다.

articles.title: AI isn't replacing SREs, it's deskilling them
articles.snippet: AI Isn't Replacing SREs. It's Deskilling Them. Observability Real Talk Subscribe Sign in AI Isn't Replacing SREs. It's Deskilling Them. When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters? Elizabeth Feb 28, 2026 22 5 3 Share 💌 Hey there, it’s Elizabeth from SigNoz! This newsletter is a n honest attempt to talk about all things - observability, OpenTelemetry, open-source and the engineering in between! & This piece took 6 days, 5 hours to be cooked, hope we served. 🌚 Subscribe There are two popular prophecies floating around tech circles these days. The first says SRE is the future of all software engineering , that as AI writes more and more code, the humans who remain will be the ones keeping systems alive. The second says AI will devour every tech job alive, SREs included. Neither is particularly useful if you’re an SRE trying to figure out what your Tuesday will look like in 2027. Let’s ask a more grounded question by looking at what’s already happening: When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters? Most of us already use AI for our daily work (our brains a little fried!), and so do SREs. Today’s discussion agenda is not whether AI replaces SREs, but whether AI is quietly making SREs less capable and whether anyone will notice anything before the next novel outage hits. The foundational framework for this entire debate comes from a 1983 research paper that’s eerily prescient. The Ironies of Automation: Part-I Note from author: Below is a brief precursor to History of Automation, which you might enjoy if you are into History and Cultures (like me 😉). In 1983, a cognitive psychologist named Lisanne Bainbridge published a paper called Ironies of Automation . It became one of the most cited papers in human factors research, and its core argument is almost uncomfortably relevant today. Bainbridge studied what happened when factories and industrial systems automated the work of blue-collar operators. The findings were paradoxical and revealed that the more you automate a process, the more critical the human operator becomes during the rare moments automation fails and the less practice they get, and the worse they become at exactly those interventions. Automation, which was inherently designed to remove humans from the loop, left them with the worst possible job, i.e., long stretches of passive monitoring punctuated by rare, high-stakes crises they were increasingly unprepared for. Ring any bells yet? 🙂 Basically, I’m drawing a parallel between the AI revolution and industrial automation. Industrial automation reshaped blue-collar work by taking over routine physical tasks, and the workers who remained had to handle exceptions they’d lost the muscle memory for. AI is doing the same thing to knowledge workers by taking over the routine cognitive tasks, the pattern matching, the triage, the known-issue resolution and leaving humans with
articles.oneLineKo: AI 자동화가 SRE 실력을 퇴화시키는 역설
articles.summaryKo: AI가 인시던트 대응의 95%를 처리하면서 SRE들이 정작 중요한 5%의 신규/복잡한 장애 대응 능력을 잃어가고 있다는 주장이다. 1983년 Lisanne Bainbridge의 'Ironies of Automation' 논문을 인용해, 자동화가 반복 작업을 없애면 인간 운영자는 드물지만 중요한 예외 상황에서 더 큰 역할을 맡게 되지만 연습 부족으로 오히려 대응 능력이 떨어진다는 역설을 설명한다. 이는 산업 자동화가 블루칼라 노동자에게 미친 영향과 AI가 지식노동자(SRE)에게 미치는 영향이 유사하다는 비유로 이어진다. 결국 AI가 SRE를 대체하는 것이 아니라 조용히 탈숙련화시키고 있다는 문제를 제기한다.

articles.title: Bunny CDN Security Incident
articles.snippet: bunny.net Status - Security update regarding one of our infrastructure providers Security update regarding one of our infrastructure providers Incident Report for bunny.net Subscribe to Updates Update We're providing an update on the reissuance of managed TLS certificates for custom domains. Reissuance is ongoing and progressing steadily. To avoid any disruption to the delivery of your content, certificates are being reissued gradually in controlled batches, and each reissued certificate uses a new private key. This is taking longer than our initial estimate, and we now expect the process to be completed by the end of October 31. Your existing certificates continue to be served without interruption until they are replaced, and no action is required from customers using managed certificates. If you manage your own TLS certificates, we continue to recommend revoking and reissuing them with new private keys as a precaution. Neither our investigation nor the provider's ongoing investigation has found any new evidence of unauthorized access to our server. We'll post a further update on our status page once reissuance is complete. If you have any questions or need help with managing your TLS certificates, our support team will be happy to assist. Posted Oct 29 , 2026 - 18:40 UTC Monitoring We're reaching out to inform you of a security incident involving one of our infrastructure providers, the steps we've taken, and what this means for you. - What happened and how we responded Last week, one of our infrastructure providers reported unauthorized access involving third-party server management software. One of our CDN nodes, located in Armenia, was hosted on a server supplied by this provider. After receiving the alert from the affected provider, our engineering team took immediate action. Within 20 minutes, we stopped routing traffic through the server. We then reviewed and preserved the relevant security logs for investigation, securely wiped the server, and revoked its access to our other systems. The affected server has been permanently removed from our infrastructure. Our investigation found no evidence of unauthorized access to the CDN node or any of its data. The infrastructure provider has also found no evidence that our server was accessed, but continues to investigate the incident. - What this means for your data While neither investigation has found any indication of unauthorized access to our server, we cannot completely rule out the possibility. If unauthorized access to our CDN node did occur, the potentially exposed information would have been: temporarily cached CDN content, Pull Zone configurations, and TLS certificates stored on that server. As an additional precaution, we have revoked and reissued all TLS certificates for bunny. net platform domains (b-cdn. net and bunny. run). Reissuance of managed TLS certificates for custom domains is ongoing and is expected to be completed within the next 24 hours. No action is required from custom

articles.title: Building an AI-native engineering org
articles.snippet: Sashank Gondala on X: "Building an AI-native engineering org" / X Article Log in Sign up Article Log in Sign up Sashank Gondala @sgondala2 3:44 PM · Oct 29, 2026 · 17.4K Views 14 30 225 495 Log in or sign up for X See what’s happening and join the conversation Continue with phone Continue with Apple Continue with Google or Log in with username or email Relevant people Sashank Gondala @ sgondala2 Follow Cofounder/CTO @furtheraicom || Past: @Apple , @GeorgiaTech , @iitbombay Trending now Terms · Privacy · Cookies · Accessibility · Ads Info · More © 2026 X Corp. Building an AI-native engineering org 5 min read Last week Will Larson ( @Lethain ) asked how leaders are evaluating engineering managers for AI skills. My reply , a list of questions to think about, got a lot of bookmarks. More broadly, I've been thinking about how to build an AI-native engineering org for a while. Sharing some lessons from the last nine months of building at FurtherAI. Part 1: What changed in how we ship How much we ship per engineer Since January, the number of code changes each engineer merges a day has grown about 5x, while our revert rate has stayed under half a percent. But giving engineers coding agents didn't get us there on its own. Every time we sped up one step, work piled up at the next. So we started going through the entire process of shipping software, one step at a time, and figuring out what we could optimize. Rebuilding the shipping process Code (March) – Agents write the code and engineers steer them. We don’t have a clean number for where this started, as early on the tools only left a mark on a change once in a while. But it’s safe to say it’s now almost 100%. Tests (April) – Agents write tests alongside code. 91% of changes now include tests, up from 15%. Review (May) – AI reviews 99% of changes before a person does, up from 60%. Human reviewers can focus on the parts that need judgment. CI (June) – We parallelized tests and run only those affected by a change. CI now runs 20× the tests in the same 17 minutes. Bug reports (July) – We've started using ClaudeTag ( @claudeai ) to automate our bug intake process. Anyone can report a bug in Slack, and ClaudeTag figures out duplicates, files a ticket, and assigns it to the right person. It now files 60% of bug tickets. Rules (August) – When a bug or a review comment exposed a rule only engineers knew, we turned it into a small Python check that runs on every commit and every PR, fails the build and prints the fix. This way, we convert tribal knowledge into rules. Agents hit these checks, fix their own code and move on. We went from zero to 21 rules. They're a big part of why low-risk changes can now merge without a person. Merging (August) – Low-risk changes that pass tests, automated checks, and AI review merge on their own. articles.oneLineKo: AI 네이티브 엔지니어링 조직 구축 9개월 경험 공유
articles.summaryKo: FurtherAI의 CTO가 지난 9개월간 코딩 에이전트를 도입해 개발 프로세스를 전면 재구축한 경험을 공유했다. 코드 작성, 테스트, 리뷰, CI, 버그 리포트, 규칙화, 머지까지 단계별로 자동화를 적용해 엔지니어 1인당 머지량이 5배 증가했고 리버트율은 0.5% 미만을 유지했다. AI 리뷰가 전체 변경의 99%를 처리하고, 저위험 변경의 최대 1/3이 사람 개입 없이 머지되며, Slack에서 에이전트에게 변경을 지시해 PR을 열 수 있는 체계까지 구축했다.

articles.title: Show GN: 컷팩(Cutfac) - Claude Code/Codex로 숏폼 만들 때 쓰는 오픈소스 비디오 에디터
articles.snippet: 저는 캡컷도 파이널컷도 쓸 줄 모릅니다. 그래도 3달 동안 Claude Code/Codex로 숏폼 300편을 만들었고, 5개 플랫폼에서 수백만 조회수가 나왔어요. 그런데 수백 편을 클로드와 코덱스 안에서만 만드는 건 여간 불편한 일이 아니더군요. 고치고 싶은 부분을 제대로 지정하기 어렵고, 프리뷰는 한 번에 하나씩밖
articles.oneLineKo: AI 코딩 도구로 숏폼 제작용 오픈소스 비디오 에디터 공개
articles.summaryKo: 제작자는 캡컷이나 파이널컷을 사용할 줄 몰랐지만, 3달간 Claude Code와 Codex만으로 숏폼 영상 300편을 만들어 수백만 조회수를 기록했다. 하지만 AI 도구 안에서만 영상을 편집하는 과정에서 수정할 부분을 정확히 지정하기 어렵고 프리뷰가 불편한 문제를 겪었다. 이를 해결하기 위해 Claude Code/Codex와 함께 쓰기 좋은 오픈소스 비디오 에디터 '컷팩(Cutfac)'을 개발해 공개했다.

articles.oneLineKo: 시스코, 27세 직원에게 무제한 AI 토큰으로 레거시 코드 재작성 맡겨
articles.summaryKo: 시스코의 사장 겸 최고제품책임자 지투 파텔은 조직 내 눈에 띄지 않던 27세 전 창업자 파드마나반 크리슈나무르티(일명 '패디')를 발탁해 시스코의 레거시 코드 98%를 재작성하는 프로젝트를 맡겼다. 패디는 EzDubs라는 실시간 번역 스타트업을 공동창업했으며, 시스코가 이를 인수하며 합류했다. 그는 단 두 명으로 구성된 팀과 무제한 AI 토큰을 활용해 레거시 코드를 리팩토링할 수 있다고 제안했고, 파텔은 이를 승인하며 '마음껏 해보라'고 전폭적으로 지원했다.

articles.summaryKo: 클라우드 플랫폼 Northflank에서 보안 침해가 발생해 모든 사용자의 환경변수가 복호화된 것으로 간주해야 한다는 경고가 발령됐다. 다수 사용자가 자신의 AI API 키가 무단 사용된 것을 확인했으며, 이는 Wiz의 'Black October' 보고서에 언급된 광범위한 AI 자격증명 공격 패턴과 일치할 수 있다. articles.title: Azure's Weakest Link – Five Full Cross-Tenant Compromises
articles.snippet: Azure's Weakest Link - Five Full Cross-Tenant Compromises Azure’s Weakest Link - Five Full Cross-Tenant Compromises | Binary Security AS Home About Careers Services Penetration Testing Application Security Security Engineering Posts Contact Azure's Weakest Link - Five Full Cross-Tenant Compromises Posted by Haakon Wik Gulbrandsrud on October 02, 2026 · 18 mins read In my previous blog posts, Azure’s Weakest Link? and Azure’s Weakest Link - Full Cross-Tenant Compromise , I gave an overview of the severely insecure architecture behind API Connections in Azure, a part of Azure Logic Apps, and an instance of a full cross-tenant compromise using these inherent flaws. Now I am back with some more vulnerabilities in this system, each giving the same primitives to the attacker. In total, the vulnerabilities here netted me a cool $200,000. I also held a talk detailing this at Blue Hat Asia 2026, and when the recordings are out, I will add a link here. TL;DR API Connections allow anyone to fully compromise any other connection worldwide, giving full access to the connected backend. This includes cross-tenant compromise of Key Vaults and Azure SQL databases, as well as any other externally connected service, such as Jira or Salesforce. The only thing stopping exploitation is really the layers of input validation bolted onto the various systems, but as you will see, it is really difficult to catch all the edge cases here. Architecture If you haven’t read the first parts of this series, I would recommend checking those out first, Azure’s Weakest Link? - Part 1 and Azure’s Weakest Link - Full Cross-Tenant Compromise , but if you don’t care, I will go through the most important parts of the architecture first. From Microsoft’s documentation , we see a quite intriguing diagram of how the API Connection architecture is built. This basically spells out all that is needed to understand how the system operates, kudos to whoever made it! It works like this A logic app, the symbol on the bottom left, queries a shared Azure API Management instance The API Management instance first checks the swagger (OpenAPI) definition of the connector type and checks that it is a valid action A sort of key exchange happens where the input token, or key, is exchanged for the configured token for the backend service The API Management instance finishes the call with this new token to the backend instance. From this, we can surmise that if we are able to trick the API Management instance to operate on a different connection than the ones we own, we would be able to effectively use the configured token for a victim’s connection on their backend service. This service can, in effect, be anything. As you can see here , the list of backend services is effectively unbounded and includes a number of Azure services. However great the diagram is, there is one crucial omission, which we have already used to great effect in part 2 of this series. By using the ARM REST API DynamicInvoke or /
articles.oneLineKo: Azure Logic Apps API Connection, 크로스테넌트 전체 탈취 5건 발견
articles.summaryKo: 보안 연구자가 Azure Logic Apps의 API Connections 아키텍처에서 다섯 건의 완전한 크로스테넌트 침해 취약점을 발견해 총 20만 달러의 포상금을 받았다. 이 취약점은 공격자가 전 세계 다른 테넌트의 API Connection을 탈취해 Key Vault, Azure SQL, Jira, Salesforce 등 연결된 백엔드 서비스에 전체 접근 권한을 얻을 수 있게 한다. API Management 인스턴스가 커넥션 소유권 검증 없이 ARM REST API의 DynamicInvoke 등을 통해 다른 테넌트의 토큰을 사용하도록 속일 수 있는 구조적 결함이 원인이다. 이는 저자의 이전 연구에 이은 후속 발견으로, Blue Hat Asia 2026에서 발표되었다.
